Monthly stipend of NT$5,000 for master's students

Monthly stipend of NT$20,000 to NT$40,000 for doctoral students, or NT$10,000 for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences or the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with a supervisor from that college
Award administered by NTHU's Office of Global Affairs

coverage: Tiered monthly stipend from NT$5,000 to NT$40,000 depending on degree level and college
application_method: Complete the online application through the NTHU International Student Online Application System, selecting 'Apply for NTHU international student scholarship'
application_route: Apply through the online international degree application system and request the scholarship during that application.
duration: Follows the duration of the degree programme enrolled in; no separate award period is published
description: The National Tsing Hua University International Student Scholarship provides a tuition and credit fee waiver plus a tiered monthly stipend to international students at NTHU, with amounts depending on the applicant's degree level and college.

not_confirmed: the archive note that China Education Association-funded and ICDF scholarship holders are ineligible, and the College of Semiconductor enrolment-year limits, neither of which appears on the page
verification.notes: Stipend by degree level, the NT$10,000 doctoral variant for the College of Humanities and Social Sciences and the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with a supervisor from that college, the tuition and credit fee waiver, the eligibility list, the application step, and the admission percentages and schedule were all read directly from NTHU's Office of Global Affairs international student admission pages. The governing document is the NTHU International Student Scholarship Regulation dated 18 April 2025. Note that the rolling admission schedule states that students who have not completed their final award examination/qualification exam or who have not graduated by 30 September 2025 cannot register in semester one.

applicant_utility: The fee waiver is the substantial part of this award: NTHU states plainly that tuition and the credit fee are waived. The monthly stipend varies sharply by level, so check which tier you fall into before you plan a budget - NT$5,000 for bachelor's and master's students, NT$20,000 to NT$40,000 for doctoral students, and NT$10,000 for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences or in the International Intercollegiate PhD Program supervised by someone from that college. There is no separate scholarship deadline: you request it inside the online international degree application by selecting 'Apply for NTHU international student scholarship', which means the scholarship decision is bound to the admission calendar. The eligibility rules around prior study in Taiwan are strict and worth reading in full, including the rule that those who previously studied in Taiwan under the foreign academic credentials regulations may reapply for a new programme only once and only for an NTHU undergraduate programme. Note also that Medicine, Dentistry and Traditional Chinese Medicine are excluded for undergraduate applicants, though graduate applicants are not affected. If you already hold another scholarship you must supply proof of it.

title: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship
university: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
deadline_central_display: No application deadline - the award is made on the basis of college recommendation and scholarship committee review
deadline_note: This scholarship is awarded on the basis of college recommendation and a review by the scholarship committee, not through an application submitted by the students. The rules are published by NYCU's Office of Student Affairs.
application_cycle: Annual award cycle managed by the scholarship committee; the department handles applications every semester
status_note: No application deadline is published because the award is nomination-based. This record is listed as upcoming by convention because NYCU does not publish a round date.
tuition_coverage_note: NYCU states the scholarship provides 'NT33,000 a month on top of a full waiver of tuition and credit fees'.
benefits: NT$33,000 per month on top of a full waiver of tuition and credit fees
Available for the first 2 years of study
In principle only one student from each college may receive the award
eligibility: New PhD students with outstanding grades who have not received scholarships, grants or subsidies from the Taiwan government

Students directly pursuing a PhD degree who wish to apply for PhD Elite Scholarships (including the MOE Elite Scholarship, Elite Ph.D. Scholarship and College Elite Ph.D. Scholarship) should submit a transcript for the scholarship application when completing registration procedures
requirements: Submit the transcript and tuition payment receipt each semester to remain eligible for the award
Award is made on the basis of college recommendation and a review by the scholarship committee
coverage: Full waiver of tuition and credit fees
application_method: Submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester through the department, which handles applications every semester
application_route: No student application: the college nominates and the scholarship committee reviews. Students should submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester through their department.
duration: The award is available for the first 2 years of study
description: The NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship provides a full waiver of tuition and credit fees plus NT$33,000 per month for the first two years of study, awarded on the basis of college recommendation and scholarship committee review rather than student application.

the exact current award amount (the source is NYCU's official scholarship regulations document, but the version located states 'Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students Award' and also mentions a separate NTD 25,000 plus NTD 8,000 matching-fund arrangement for other awards, so the regulation version should be confirmed with the university)

verification.notes: The NT$33,000 monthly amount and full tuition and credit fee waiver for the first 2 years come from NYCU's official scholarship regulations document hosted on an nycu.edu.tw domain. The NYCU Office of International Affairs scholarships page confirms that PhD-level scholarship amounts are flexibly adjusted based on the University's actual budget and the national special circumstances, so the figure should be verified against the current regulations. The award is described as nomination-based rather than student-applied, which explains why no application deadline is published.

applicant_utility: You cannot apply for this one yourself - NYCU makes it on the basis of college recommendation and a review by the scholarship committee, so the practical route is doing well enough in your first year to be noticed by your department. If you win it you get NT$33,000 a month on top of a full waiver of tuition and credit fees for your first two years of doctoral study, which is one of the more generous doctoral packages in Taiwan. Two things to keep in mind. In principle only one student from each college receives it, so the competition is internal and fierce. And NYCU's Office of International Affairs notes that PhD scholarship amounts are flexibly adjusted based on the university's budget and national circumstances, so confirm the current figure with your college before treating NT$33,000 as fixed. Even if you hold this award, submit your transcript and tuition payment receipt each semester - NYCU requires this to retain eligibility, and it applies equally to those on MOE Elite and College Elite PhD awards.
